cohort: 707 newborn children from the 2006-2011 birth cohorts of the German Socio-Economic Panel Study (SOEP)
finding: The likelihood of cesarean delivery increased for women with the least education only when they faced constraints in accessing hospital care, suggesting that high access to care might mitigate educational disparities in birth outcomes.
mod_finding: This study found that women with the least education were more likely to have a cesarean delivery when they had limited access to hospital care, suggesting that access to care may contribute to social disparities in mode of delivery.
